unit.why: A short quoted report of how R. Menahem Azariah of Fano died a 'death by a kiss': his soul bound itself above and he fell dead to the ground. The passing of the Hasidic R. Michel is likened to it in one closing line.
unit.boundary_note: The division opens mid-compilation ('ובס׳ ע״ה') and seems to continue the previous division's theme of devekut. The trailing heading 'מענין דגים' belongs to the next division.

stories.start_quote: ושמעתי וקבלתי ממגידי אמת שמיתת הרמ״ע מפאנו
stories.end_quote: הסתלקות של הה״ק ר״ר מיכלי זצל"ה
stories.summary_en: The author of Ets ha-Da'at Tov reports a tradition that the Rama of Fano died a death by a kiss: his soul cleaved on high and he fell to the earth like a stone. He prays for such an end, and the passing of R. Michel is said to have been the same.

tags.why: The whole account is the manner of a sage's death.

quotes: ונפל לארץ מושלך כאבן דומם ונשאר מת על הארץ
tags.why: The death is described as an event.
It praises a pre-Hasidic kabbalist, the Rama of Fano, and is quoted from an earlier book.
He dies in a state of the soul cleaving on high.
A mystical cleaving that ends in death by a kiss.
Framed as an oral tradition received from reliable tellers.
